newsitem.title: JAPAN: ASIAN SUGAR - Thai raw premiums down, China quiet.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN SUGAR - Thai raw premiums down, China quiet.

text.p: Premiums for Thai raw sugar for shipment in the March to May period of 1997 are falling further as China is not expected to buy sugar in the market until at least next April, local traders in Tokyo said on Thursday.

Cargoes of Thai raw sugar for March/May delivery are being quoted at 0.65 cents over New York March futures contracts on a free-on-board (FOB) basis, down from 0.7 to 0.75 cents last week, traders said. Premiums for January/March and May/July delivery are being quoted at 1.0 cent above New York's March contract and 0.80 to 0.85 cents over May, respectively.

"Western traders and sugar mills in Thailand are looking for importers. But we can't find active buyers at the moment, and Thai raw premiums are falling further," a sugar trader at a Tokyo-based trade house said.
Japanese traders said they had earlier expected China to start buying Thai sugar as early as in January/March.

"But sugar prices in China are still too low, and some import restriction is necessary to protect local farmers. I think a level of 5,000 yuan will be a target for the Chinese government," another Tokyo sugar trader said.
Chinese authorities are unlikely to issue sugar import licences unless domestic prices recover to around 5,000 yuan ($602), traders said.

Sugar prices in Shanghai are currently at around 4,300 yuan ($518) a tonne, and they are lower in producer areas, the state-owned Shanghai Sugar and Tobacco General Co said. Prices in Beijing and in Nanning, capital of Guangxi Province, were also 4,300 yuan per tonne.
Chinese sugar imports during the January-August period of this year slumped by 54.9 percent from the same period a year ago to 830,000 tonnes, customs data showed.
Cuba has long-term contracts with China to export about 400,000 tonnes of raw sugar a year, and could ship up to 200,000 in 1995, local traders said.
"We're not sure how many tonnes of sugar will be shipped this year. But Cuba is not required to pay a penalty even if it fails to meet the commitment," another trader said.
For sugar from the southern hemisphere, local importers are covering Australian raw sugar for shipment early next year, the traders said.
Fiji Sugar Marketing was rumoured this week to be close to fixing its order for 15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Fiji to Japan at a rate near $22. But the details could not be confirmed.

The South Africa Sugar Association was said to have fixed 25,000 tonnes in bulk from Durban to Japan for September/October dates but details of the rate have yet to emerge, London traders said this week. South African sugar is coming to Japan on schedule so far, the traders said.
They cited a rumour that a Japanese trade house, which steered clear of importing South African sugar in the late 1980s due to economic sanctions, would be back in the business soon.
